newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rattled by earnings warnings.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rattled by earnings warnings.

text.p: Stocks closed lower Wednesday after technology companies' warnings about their profits cooled some of the optimism about corporate earnings for the latest quarter.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended down 42.07 points at 7,718.71, its third straight session of losses. In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,294 to 1,192 on moderate volume of 492 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

Warnings by personal computer manufacturer Gateway 2000 Inc. that its second-quarter revenues would be about even with the first quarter and computer disk drive maker Seagate Technology Inc. of disappointing quarterly revenues raised concerns that trouble might lie ahead for the technology sector.
Seagate lost 5-1/4 to 36-1/4 and Gateway fell 1-3/4 to 32 in consolidated trading.
The earnings warnings sparked concern that the entire sector, which has run up during the past month, and possibly the broader market might suffer.
"There's been some suspicion that if there's no inflation ahead, we might have a slowdown, which would hurt earnings generally," said Harry Laubscher, an analyst at Tucker Anthony.

Some analysts waved off the earnings warnings, saying the sell-off was a knee-jerk reaction, noting that in the weeks leading up to the earnings reporting season, the stock market is often rocked by cautionary statements from companies.
"We are telling people to be very very cautious. Start taking some profits and buy bonds for safety," Laubscher said.

Gary Loe, an analyst for Anderson & Loe, a firm that advises money managers, said, "Some consolidation in stocks is certainly reasonable after the gains we've had. But my sense is we're in a very volatile period."
That volatility is expected to get stronger through the week as Friday's "triple witching" expiration of options and futures nears.
Computer giant International Business Machines Corp. lost 7/8 to 89.
Disney Corp. fell 1-1/2 to 82-1/2 after Southern Baptists said they would boycott Disney and its subsidiaries, citing the firm's "gay-friendly" policies.

Tobacco stocks fell on fears that a settlement being negotiated by the industry, the public health community, and state attorneys general would collapse. Philip Morris shed 5/8 to 45-1/2 and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp. was down 1/2 at 34-1/2.
Some stocks bucked the trend depite the overall softness. Jabil Circuit Inc. jumped 13-3/8 to 82-1/4 after it posted strong earnings and set a two-for-one stock split.
American Express Co. rose 1-1/2 to 77-7/8 on takeover rumours.
Also stronger was Allied Signal Inc., which gained 1 to 83 after the aerospace company agreed to buy Grimes Aerospace Co., a maker of aircraft lighting systems.
In its initial public offering, Boston Properties Inc. added 1-3/4 to 26-3/4 in heavy trading.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 10.68 points to 1,432.43.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 5.36 to 889.06. The American Stock Exchange index edged up 0.11 to 625.97.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 1.68 to 463.41. The average share was down 16 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 8,399.174, down 35.258 or 1.42 percent.
